title: Watch succession pocket log - lilypad shift 2027-11-23
content:
Summary:

03:12-07:40 UTC watch (Lilypad) covering EU->global traffic. This log captures a brief, noisy latency surge tied to a KV cache regression introduced by the 2027-11-23 canary deploy (infra/kv-cache:2.7.1). Impact: p95 token latency for text/generate rose from ~220ms -> ~2.3s for ~35 minutes; error rate (5xx) climbed from 0.6% -> 3.1% at peak. A subset of hosted API requests experienced persistent cold-starts (replayable by requests with long prompt prefixes).

Timeline (concise):
- 03:14 UTC: First alert - p95 tokens up, alert from host-api/perf-p95.
- 03:16 UTC: Pager to oncall (Ravi). Began triage: confirmed increased latency and decreased KV cache hit-rate on metrics.kv_prefix_hit (global) down from ~87% -> ~41%.
- 03:22 UTC: Canary services still reporting low hit-rate; autoscaler did not scale up as expected (ops-metrics showed missing aggregated label 'env=canary' after job rename).
- 03:28 UTC: Rolled back canary to infra/kv-cache:2.7.0 (hotfix rollback).
- 03:33 UTC: Manually restarted kv-cache pods in eu-west and forced cache-rewarmers (see commands below). Hit-rate recovered to ~78% by 03:45 UTC.
- 03:48 UTC: Enabled emergency-scaling policy to allow temporary oversubscription to dedicated capacity; routed ~30% traffic to dedicated-eu pool to relieve burst pressure.
- 04:05 UTC: Observed p95 back to ~260ms, error rate returning to baseline.
- 07:40 UTC: Handoff to morning watch (Elena). Post-incident actions created and owners assigned.

Immediate mitigations performed (what we did):
- Reverted canary to previous image (infra/kv-cache:2.7.0).
- Manual restart of kv-cache replicas: kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -n hosted-eu-west (03:33 UTC).
- Forced cache-rewarm job: jobs/cache-rewarm -e eu-west -p 900s (03:35 UTC) to repopulate prefixes used by high-volume routes.
- Temporary traffic reroute: updated routing-rule:traffic-shift-urgent to send 30% to dedicated-eu.
- Temporary alerting tweak: increased sensitivity window on host-api/perf-p95 to reduce noisy paging during rewarm (reverted later).

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis:
- The canary build infra/kv-cache:2.7.1 introduced a labeling change in its Prometheus exporter (label name change: 'env' -> 'env_name'), which broke the autoscaler's Prom metrics aggregation query. Because the autoscaler was not seeing the expected aggregated load metric, it did not scale up during the latency spike, amplifying cold-cache effects. The new binary also had a subtle TTL miscalculation when rewarm jobs race with eviction windows, increasing cold start likelihood.

Runbook updates (draft changes to be made before next deploy):
1) Add a preflight test for Prom exporter label stability: unit/integ test that ensures metrics labels match autoscaler queries.
2) Add explicit post-deploy sanity checks (automated): check kv_prefix_hit >= 80% within 5 minutes of deploy on a 10k synthetic warmup workload; if not, auto-rollback.
3) Rework cache-rewarm job to use idempotent rewarm tokens and extend grace TTL by +30s in 2.7.x lineage.
4) Autoscaler: don't rely on single label name; support fallback queries or a safe default scale action if metric absent for >60s.
5) Add a runbook section for 'prefix leak / low hit-rate' with commands and sample queries (see playbook snippet below).

Playbook snippet (for inclusion in runbook section):
- Check global KV prefix hit: grafana/dashboard/kv-cache -> kv_prefix_hit (rollup: 1m).
- If kv_prefix_hit < 60% AND p95 tokens > 1s:
  * Step 1: Confirm active deploy (kubectl -n hosted get pods -l app=kv-cache --show-labels).
  * Step 2: Rollback canary (kubectl -n hosted set image deployment/kv-cache kv-cache=infra/kv-cache:2.7.0) OR disable rollout.
  * Step 3: kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -n <region> (start with eu-west).
  * Step 4: trigger jobs/cache-rewarm -e <region> --synthetic=top-200-prompts
  * Step 5: If autoscaler not scaling, check prometheus query used by autoscaler and look for missing labels ([check query in infra/alerts/autoscaler.yaml]).
  * Escalation: If no improvement in 10m, route 25-50% traffic to dedicated pools and notify Solutions Eng.

Commands used (copyable):
- kubectl -n hosted set image deployment/kv-cache kv-cache=infra/kv-cache:2.7.0
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -n hosted-eu-west
- jobs/cache-rewarm --region=eu-west --prompts=top-1000 --concurrency=8
- curl -sS 'https://prom:9090/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(kv_prefix_hit[1m])' | jq .

Outstanding follow-ups (owners):
- CON-2143 (Maya) - Add exporter label compatibility tests + CI gate.
- OPS-1192 (Jordan) - Autoscaler: implement fallback metric query and add alert if metric missing >60s.
- DOC-332 (Ravi) - Draft runbook section for 'KV prefix cold starts' with playbook snippet above (due 2027-11-26).
- ENG-1289 (Elena) - Rewarm job: make idempotent and add TTL buffer; coordinate with release engineering (due 2027-11-30).

Notes / Misc observations:
- This incident was noisy because two failures aligned: a labeling change + too-tight TTLs. The revert alone reduced error rate but rewarm + manual routing brought latency back quickly.
- Observability gap: autoscaler uses a single Prom query without a defensive fallback; add a SLO/alert that verifies the autoscaler metric ingestion pipeline (end-to-end) on every deploy.
- Communication: sent short incident update to #sre-ops and product-incident channel at 04:15 UTC. Drafted postmortem candidate flag (pending review).

Handoff to next watch (Elena) at 07:40 UTC:
- State: stable, p95 ~260-300ms, kv_prefix_hit ~80%.
- Expectation: monitor target routes for 24h for recurrence. If pattern reoccurs during high volume windows, escalate to oncall rotation lead and Solutions Eng for capacity plan.
- Quick checklist for next watch:
  * Verify CON-2143 test landed in CI.
  * Confirm autoscaler fallback PR is in review or scheduled (OPS-1192).
  * Keep rewarm job runbook item accessible in pagerduty playbook.

Appendix: short tips for next oncall (notes to self):
- When seeing low kv_prefix_hit, check recent deploys in last 30m first. Label-only changes are common cause.
- If autoscaler not reacting, check Prom scrape/aggregation labels before rolling your own scale commands.
- Avoid toggling alerting windows unless coordinating with SRE lead; prefer silencing specific noisy alert instances.

End of shift log.
